title: Cipher and Portrait
premise: When the coffin of town founder Edmund Vasse is exhumed for a centennial reburial and found empty, cathedral archivist Isandro Crane becomes the prime suspect — the only man with keys to the crypt. To clear his name, Isandro decodes a ledger disguised as a baptismal register, revealing that Vasse never died in 1909: he faked his death after a murder, and a line of respected townsfolk have guarded the secret ever since. As Isandro follows the ledger's cipher through wills, portraits, and parish records, he discovers the current custodian of the secret is killing to keep it buried. In the end Isandro must choose between exposing the truth that will destroy the town's founding families and protecting the one person who showed him loyalty — and he chooses truth, at the cost of everything he spent fifteen years preserving.
about_author: Coral Winterbourne is a former parish records clerk from coastal Maine who spent a decade cataloguing documents no one was supposed to read. She writes mysteries about quiet people who know too much.

chapters.title: The Weight of Dust
chapters.summary: Isandro Crane's POV. A day in the life of the cathedral archivist: filing, cataloguing, keeping the crypt's single iron key on a chain around his neck. Establishes his obsessive order and loneliness. The chapter ends with the centennial committee's letter announcing Edmund Vasse's exhumation. Emotional beat: contentment shadowed by dread.

chapters.title: An Empty Box
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The exhumation draws half the town to the cemetery. When the coffin is opened before witnesses, it holds only river stones weighted to a body's approximate mass. The sheriff's eyes go straight to Isandro — the keyholder. Emotional beat: public humiliation; the ordered world cracks open.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Keys
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV under interrogation. He recounts every person who has accessed the crypt since 2010, but his meticulous logs show gaps — three entries torn out, in a hand too like his own. Sheriff Delia Marsh, fair but pressured, releases him as a suspect of convenience. Emotional beat: betrayal by his own records.

chapters.title: The Baptismal Ledger
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Searching for evidence someone forged his log, he notices the old baptismal register's dates are impossible — baptisms recorded years before births. Marginal numerals form a pattern. He photographs pages, heart pounding. Emotional beat: the thrill of a scholar realizing the archive itself is lying.

chapters.title: Portrait of a Founder
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Isandro and Maren Vasse-Holt, the founder's great-granddaughter, a restorer preparing the portrait unveiled at the centennial. Under raking light she finds pigment over an earlier inscription. Isandro visits her studio; two lonely perfectionists recognize each other. Emotional beat: cautious alliance forming.

chapters.title: What the Numbers Say
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The marginal numerals decode against the ledger's page numbers into names and sums — payments made annually since 1909 to families still in town. The first payment's recipient line reads 'E.V., being alive.' Emotional beat: vertigo; the founder may have walked out of his own grave.

chapters.title: The First Custodian
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. She researches her family papers and finds letters suggesting Edmund Vasse killed a business partner, Josiah Pell, then staged his death with the coroner's help. Her grandfather's diary calls the arrangement 'our covenant.' Emotional beat: inherited guilt; love of family curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: A Death in the Stacks
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The cathedral's elderly sexton, Ambrose — the last person who might remember the crypt's older rituals — is found dead at the foot of the archive stairs. Ruled an accident. Isandro finds Ambrose's broom laid across the ledger shelf like a warning. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into fear.

chapters.title: Sheriff Marsh's Doubt
chapters.summary: Delia Marsh's POV. She reopens the case quietly, troubled by the stairwell evidence and by pressure from the town council to close it fast. She shares an off-record file with Isandro: the original 1909 coroner's report is missing from state archives. Emotional beat: two investigators learning to trust across institutional lines.

chapters.title: The Covenant Families
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Cross-referencing the decoded payments, he maps five dynasties — Vasse, Holt, Merrick, Okafor-Lund, and Pell — whose fortunes all date to 1910. The Pells, supposedly extinct, have one living descendant: a night nurse named Ruth Pell. Emotional beat: the past revealed as a living architecture.

chapters.title: Ruth Pell Knows
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. She tends the dying matriarch Ada Merrick, who murmurs fragments about 'the second coffin' and 'the boy in the river.' Ruth admits to Isandro that her family has received anonymous envelopes every January for a century — hush money for a murder they didn't commit but must forever mourn. Emotional beat: the price of survival made flesh.

chapters.title: Second Coffin
chapters.summary: Isandro and Maren's POV, alternating. Following Ada's fragment, they find a sealed secondary vault beneath the crypt's flagstones containing Josiah Pell's actual remains — moved there decades ago, along with Edmund Vasse's true grave goods, including a confession letter. Someone has been there recently; the seal is freshly cut. Emotional beat: awe turning to terror — they are not alone in this knowledge.

chapters.title: The Confession Letter
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The letter confirms Edmund murdered Josiah to conceal embezzlement that built the town, then bought his own death. It names a rotating 'Custodian' sworn to maintain the fiction. Maren realizes her own father held the office until his death last year — and that the succession passed somewhere. Emotional beat: filial love and horror intertwined.

chapters.title: Someone in the Archive
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Returning at night, he surprises an intruder among the shelves — a figure he recognizes by gait but not face. Chased through the stacks, he escapes with a torn coat button and a concussion. The next morning, pages of the baptismal ledger are missing. Emotional beat: the hunter becomes the hunted inside his own sanctuary.

chapters.title: Delia Closes In
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Forensics on Ambrose's death reveal a push, not a fall. Delia narrows suspects to those with crypt access across generations and confronts councilman Aldous Merrick, whose alibi is suspiciously perfect. That night her office is ransacked and the 1909 file stolen. Emotional beat: justice within the law beginning to fail.

chapters.title: The Button and the Portrait
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Cleaning the Vasse portrait further, she discovers a later overpainting hiding a second figure beside Edmund — the current Custodian's traditional inclusion, updated each generation. The face matches Aldous Merrick. She brings the button Isandro found; it fits Merrick's coat. Emotional beat: revelation as heartbreak — Merrick mentored them both.

chapters.title: Offered a Place in the File
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Merrick invites Isandro to tea and offers him the Custodianship: protection, funding for the archive, silence. He frames it as mercy — the town's peace, hundreds of livelihoods, all resting on one old crime. Isandro asks for a night to decide. Emotional beat: temptation rendered genuinely reasonable; loyalty versus truth embodied.

chapters.title: What Isandro Keeps
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. Merrick, sensing exposure, moves to eliminate loose ends: Ruth is attacked at the care home and survives because Ada Merrick herself intervenes, confessing aloud before nurses. Ada's deathbed testimony is recorded. Ruth calls Isandro with one sentence: 'He's coming for the ledger tonight.' Emotional beat: courage passing between the powerless.

chapters.title: The Crypt at Midnight
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Climax begins. Merrick comes to burn the archive; Isandro lures him into the crypt and locks the iron door with his own key, forcing a confrontation above Josiah Pell's bones. Merrick confesses to Ambrose's death and the thefts while Delia, tipped off, takes him into custody below ground. Emotional beat: the archivist weaponizes order itself.

chapters.title: Reading the Names Aloud
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. At a stormy town meeting, Isandro reads the decoded ledger publicly — every payment, every signature, the confession letter entered as evidence. Families rage; some thank him. Maren stands beside him, renouncing her inheritance's silence clause. Emotional beat: catharsis; truth as communal wound and cleansing.

chapters.title: Reburial
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Josiah Pell is buried properly, with Ruth delivering the eudogy her family was denied for a century. The empty Vasse coffin is interred with a new marker reading only 'Here lies a story we finally told.' Isandro resigns as archivist, handing Delia the complete, unaltered logs. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into restitution.

chapters.title: Cipher and Portrait
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Isandro's POV. Months later, Isandro restores the Vasse portrait with Maren, leaving both figures visible — founder and partner, crime and consequence. He begins writing a true history of the town, knowing some doors won't open to him again. The final image: the crypt key melted down into a small bell that rings when the archive door opens. Emotional beat: hard-won peace at the price of belonging.
